paragraphs.heading: What happened
paragraphs.text: Krakatoa was a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait, in what was then the Dutch East Indies and is now Indonesia. It erupted from 19 May to 21 October 1883, a span of more than five months. The most significant eruption came on 27 August. It destroyed over 70% of the island and the archipelago around it, and the island collapsed into a caldera. The eruption and the tsunamis it created are blamed for at least 36,417 deaths.

paragraphs.heading: The first weeks
paragraphs.text: In the years before 1883, seismic activity around the volcano was intense, and earthquakes were felt as far off as the Australian Northern Territory. In May 1883, steam began venting regularly from Perboewatan. The island had three cones, and this was the northernmost. Ash rose to an estimated 6 kilometres. The explosions could be heard 160 km away in Batavia, today's Jakarta, where they rattled windows and doors. Dust fell 480 km away.

paragraphs.heading: A summer of growing violence
paragraphs.text: After the first burst the eruptions soon quietened. They picked up strength again on 19 June. The eruptions went on through July and kept getting more violent until the explosions of 27 August. Tides nearby ran unusually high, and anchored ships needed chains to moor them. In early August a Dutch engineer who landed on the island found a layer of ash about 50 cm thick and all vegetation destroyed, with only tree stumps left. He advised against any further landings.

paragraphs.heading: 26 August
paragraphs.text: The eruption entered its climactic phase at about 1:00 pm on 26 August. By 2:00 pm a black cloud of ash could be seen 27 km high. The eruption was almost continuous, with explosions heard every ten minutes, and by 5:00 pm they were audible all over Java. Ships within 20 km of the volcano reported heavy ash fall and pieces of hot pumice up to 10 cm across landing on their decks. Between 7:00 and 8:00 pm a small tsunami reached the shores of Java and Sumatra, 40 km away.

paragraphs.heading: 27 August
paragraphs.text: The climax was a series of eleven enormous explosions on 27 August. The first, at 5:30 am, was at Perboewatan and set off a tsunami. Krakatau exploded again at 6:44 am at Danan, and that tsunami spread east and west. The third explosion, at 10:02 am, was the largest. The eruption of that day had an estimated volcanic explosivity index of 6, and in recorded history it ranks among the deadliest and most destructive volcanic events.

paragraphs.heading: The loudest sound
paragraphs.text: The third explosion is the loudest sound that has ever been measured. People heard it in Perth, Western Australia, 3,110 km away, and on the island of Rodrigues near Mauritius, 4,800 km away. On Rodrigues the blast was taken for cannon fire from a nearby ship. The pressure wave went around the globe more than three times. Yet close to the volcano, the largest explosions were much less noticeable to the ear, or were not heard at all.
